'''''Juniperus canariensis''''' is a woody plant in the family [[Cupressaceae]] [[native plant|native]] to the [[Canary Islands]] and [[Madeira]], off the coast of Northwestern Africa.<ref name=POWO/><ref name=Mazur2021/>

The species was previously treated as part of ''[[Juniperus phoenicea]]'', which is now regarded as restricted to [[Spain]] and [[France]], and later, as ''J. phoenicea'' was split into ''J. phoenicea'' and ''[[Juniperus turbinata|J. turbinata]]'', as part of ''J. turbinata'', which is found throughout the [[Mediterranean]] and in the [[Arabian Peninsula]].<ref name=Romo2019/>

Studies published in 2017 and 2018 on the genetic<ref name=Jiménez2017/><ref name=Sánchez-Gómez2018/> and morphological<ref name=Mazur2018/> differences found within the ''J. phoenicea'' [[species complex]] showed that the [[Macaronesia|Macaronesian]] population merited a status equivalent to that of ''J. phoenicea'' (''[[sensu stricto]]'') and ''J. turbinata''.<ref name=Romo2019/>
